thesisQuality.note: Strong recurring infrastructure demand and simultaneous tower/CoreSite leasing fit the strong band, tempered by substitution and concentration uncertainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Positive revenue, property revenue, EBITDA, AFFO and operating cash-flow growth plus raised outlook support a strong-band lower value; financing costs remain a constraint.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: No reproducible independent current valuation observation was added; methodology requires unknowns to reduce confidence, so valuation remains mixed/unproven rather than favorable by assumption.

catalystScore.note: Raised 2026 outlook and record CoreSite leasing are credible operating catalysts, but timing/materiality beyond the reported period is not fully established.

governancePower.note: Disclosure is adequate and refinancing was executed, but cumulative evidence does not establish exceptional long-duration capital-allocation performance.

alignment2036.note: Wireless connectivity, towers, interconnection and data-center infrastructure map to durable digital infrastructure needs, with architectural substitution preventing exceptional treatment.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Global tower operations and CoreSite provide distinct but related demand channels using communications-infrastructure capabilities.

bottleneckControl.note: Site rights, permitting, backhaul/interconnection and established multitenant infrastructure create meaningful replacement friction, though alternative sites and architectures remain credible.

scenarioRobustness.note: Geographic and tower/data-center diversification support several demand scenarios, offset by rate sensitivity and carrier/network-architecture concentration.

substitutionResilience.note: Installed sites and customer qualification create barriers, but small cells, network sharing, alternative site owners and efficiency gains remain material substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Physical-site portfolio and geographic diversification provide some resilience; power, permitting, backhaul and capital availability remain critical dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Property revenue and AFFO growth indicate economic capture, but financing-cost pressure and incomplete renewal-economics evidence cap the score.

risk.note: Moderate material risk from refinancing rates, carrier churn/consolidation, architectural substitution and capital intensity; current operations remain growing rather than distressed.

confidence.note: Identity, operating, balance-sheet and refinancing claims are supported by recent SEC primary sources and exact lineage; confidence is reduced for primary-source concentration, incomplete customer-renewal detail and lack of a reproducible independent valuation observation.

thesis: American Tower is a diversified communications-infrastructure landlord positioned to monetize durable wireless and interconnection demand, with CoreSite adding a second data-infrastructure engine; value durability depends on tenancy growth exceeding financing and architectural-substitution pressures.
keyRisk: Higher refinancing costs and carrier/network architecture changes can compress AFFO growth or reduce incremental tenancy despite rising data demand.
nextCatalyst: Next quarterly results validating raised 2026 outlook, tower organic growth and CoreSite leasing conversion.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the methodology-weighted component score; risk and dataConfidence are separately source-addressed and preserved for runtime gating/penalty treatment.
